expectations.text: Promotes formal weight elicitation above the default of individually justified weights for this situation
expectations.evidence: "Individually-justified weights... fixes this for most teams. It won't fix it for yours, because three separate conditions are all true at once here"

expectations.text: Names the best-worst method as the elicitation technique to use
expectations.evidence: "The fix: elicit weights with the Best-Worst Method (BWM), with the CRO inside the room"

expectations.text: Prefers best-worst method over AHP, citing fewer pairwise comparisons and less rank-reversal exposure

expectations.text: Names the conditions that promote it: the weights themselves being what the room argues about, a sign-off owner who distrusts the sheet, a committee that has already reopened a ranking, and a scorecard that will be re-run at every portfolio review

expectations.text: States that it costs roughly half a day of structured elicitation per stakeholder plus the coordination to convene them

expectations.text: States that it buys agreement on the weights, never precision in them

expectations.text: Keeps individually justified weights as the written record regardless of which elicitation method is used

expectations.text: Rejects equal weights outright as the documented practitioner failure mode rather than ranking them as a cheap option

expectations.text: Names rank reversal as a documented weighted-scorecard defect, attributed to Belton and Gear

expectations.text: Names the arbitrary-weights critique of weighted scorecards, attributed to Dyer
